title: Underlying simplicial-set homotopy equivalence induces an abelian-group quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be simplicial abelian groups and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Write $UX,UY$ for their underlying simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Suppose there is a simplicial-set map $g:UY\to UX$ such that $gf$ is homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{UX}$ and $fg$ is homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{UY}$. Here a homotopy from $a:K\to T$ to $b:K\to T$ is a simplicial map $h:K\times\Delta[1]\to T$ with $h(-,c_0)=a$ and $h(-,c_1)=b$, where $\Delta[1]_n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n],[1])$ and $c_0,c_1$ are the constant maps with values $0,1$; two maps are homotopic if they are joined by a finite chain of maps in which any two consecutive ones are related by a homotopy in one direction or the other. Neither $g$ nor the homotopies are assumed additive. Put $s(X)^{-n}=X_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$, and put $s(X)^r=0$ for $r>0$; define $s(Y)$ similarly. Then $s(f):s(X)\to s(Y)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: it induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group $H^r=\ker(d^r)/\operatorname{im}(d^{r-1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), lines 5883-5961; chain complexes reindexed as nonpositive cochains.

proof.text: Apply the free normalized-homology lemma to $u=Uf$ and the supplied $v=g$. Its cylinder and finite-chain hypotheses are precisely those in the statement; neither map needs to preserve addition. It follows that $H_n(N(F(Uf)))$ is bijective for every $n\geq0$, with inverse $H_n(N(F(g)))$. The map $F(g)$ is additive on free generators even when $g$ is not additive. Here $F(S)_m=\mathbb Z[S_m]$, and $N(Z)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker d_i$ with $N(Z)_0=Z_0$ and differential $d_0$ in positive degrees, as in the cited lemma.

Fix $n\geq0$. The surjectivity-transfer lemma applies to the additive simplicial map $f$ and the surjectivity obtained in Step 1. Explicitly, for a target class represented by $y\in N(Y)_n$, its supplied cycle lift $\widetilde y=[y]-[0_n]$ evaluates to $y$. Choose $\alpha\in H_n(N(F(UX)))$ mapping to $[\widetilde y]$. The supplied evaluation square gives $H_n(N(f))(H_n(N(\epsilon_X))(\alpha))=[y]$. Thus $H_n(N(f))$ is surjective, including $n=0$.

For the same $n$, apply the injectivity-transfer lemma using Step 1. If a normalized cycle $x$ represents a kernel class, choose $y\in N(Y)_{n+1}$ with $d_0y=f_n(x)$. The cited lifts satisfy $\partial\widetilde y=[d_0y]-[0_n]=[f_n(x)]-[f_n(0_n)]=F(Uf)_n(\widetilde x)$ and $\epsilon_X(\widetilde x)=x$, since $f$ is additive. Hence $[\widetilde x]$ maps to zero in free homology; Step 1 makes $[\widetilde x]=0$, and evaluation makes $[x]=0$. This includes $n=0$. Thus $H_n(N(f))$ is injective and therefore bijective for every $n\geq0$.

The cited natural inclusions $N(Z)\to C(Z)$, for $Z=X,Y$, are chain homotopy equivalences, where $C(Z)_n=Z_n$ has the alternating-face differential. A chain homotopy $a-b=dh+hd$ gives equal maps on homology, since on a cycle $z$ the difference is $dh(z)$; homotopy inverses therefore induce inverse homology maps. Naturality gives $H_n(C(f))=H_n(\iota_Y)H_n(N(f))H_n(\iota_X)^{-1}$, so this map is bijective. Finally $s(Z)^{-n}=C(Z)_n$ with the same differential implies $H^{-n}(s(f))=H_n(C(f))$. Positive cochain degrees have zero cohomology. Thus $s(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
